generation.explanation: At each peg of a Galton board, a ball bounces left or right with probability ½ (or p, if you tilt it with the slider). After n rows, the bin it lands in is just the number of right-bounces k. There are C(n,k) different paths that end in bin k, so the probability of landing there is C(n,k)·pᵏ(1−p)ⁿ⁻ᵏ, which is the binomial distribution. The blue histogram shows the share of balls in each bin. As more balls drop, it settles onto the red theoretical binomial curve (law of large numbers). With many rows, that curve looks like a bell curve.
